questions.question:
Select the correct option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution'.

It is __more hot now.__
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** option (3)** i.e. **"hotter now".** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"more hot now__**" is grammatically incorrect. It should be **"hotter now."**
 
• **‘hot’** is an adjective. It has three degrees. **Hot** (positive), **Hotter **(comparative) and **Hottest **(superlative).
 
• The adjectives that have comparative forms **do not need to add ‘more’ before them.**
 __
 
• **For example: Better (CORRECT), More good (INCORRECT), Quicker (CORRECT), More quick (INCORRECT).**
 
 
 
• Hence, the correct answer is "hotter now".

Therefore the correct sentence is " It is hotter now__". [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The adjectives that do not have any comparative forms** need to add ‘more’ before them.** Generally, adjectives with two or more than two syllables take more before them.

 
 
• **For example: Beautiful- More beautiful**. **Boring- More boring. **

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Your work __diary will of benefit__ if you use it and keep all the information updated.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option (3)** i.e. **"diary will be of benefit".** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"diary will of benefit"__ ** is grammatically incorrect. There must be a main verb after '**will**'.
 
• Option 3) **"diary will be of benefit"** is grammatically correct and carries the proper meaning that the diary will provide a benefit or be advantageous if used and kept updated.
 
• Hence, **option (3)** is the most appropriate to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Therefore, the correct sentence is *"**Your work __diary will be of benefit __if you use it and keep all the information updated"*. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Let's check why the other options are not appropriate to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
 
 
• **Option 1 "diary will benefit of"** is grammatically incorrect; "benefit from" would be proper but still implies that the diary itself benefits, which doesn't fit.
 
• **Option 2 "diary will benefitted"** incorrectly uses the **past tense verb "benefitted" without an auxiliary verb,** and wrongly suggests the diary itself benefits.
 
• **Option 4 "diary of benefit"** is a sentence fragment **without a verb**, it lacks completeness, not fully conveying the meaning as the original sentence.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Smith will / be learning / French when / they are arriving.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'they are arriving'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The tense used in the sentence is the **Future Continuous** tense where we use '**will be + present participle**' ("be learning" in this case). This tense is used to describe an ongoing or unfinished action in the future.
 
• When using '**when**' in sentences with Future Continuous tense, the clause that follows '**when**' should be in the **Simple Present** tense to describe a future action or situation.
 
• The phrase '**they are arriving**' is an improper use of the **Present Continuous** tense in the context of this sentence. The correct usage would be the Simple Present tense – '**they arrive**'.
 
• The correct sentence would be "*Smith will be learning French when** they arrive***".

Therefore, the correct answer is** Option 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The concept involved in identifying this grammatical error is understanding tense agreement, which refers to the matching of the tenses in a sentence to maintain consistency and proper chronological description of events.

__
 
• Yet Wallace, who was an (5) ____, had been working far away in the Malay Archipelago, whilst Darwin had not left England for several years.
 
• From the passage, it is clear that Wallace was also researching the problem of species. He had been working far away in the Malay Archipelago. It means he was travelling here and there to collect the matter.
 
• **‘explorer’ (अन्वेषक)** - A person who explores an unfamiliar area; an adventurer.
 
• Hence, ‘explorer’ is the most appropriate to fill in the blank.

**Therefore, the correct sentence is **Darwin planned to (1) ***write ***__a book describing his (2) __***discoveries***__. He sent Darwin an essay which almost word for word repeated Darwin's own ideas. Yet Wallace, who was an (5) __***explorer ***__had been working far away in the Malay Archipelago, whilst Darwin had not left England for several years.
